messages:
Liam O'Connor: Heads-up: noticed partner credits from BenchLabs were applied against lp-gpu-west usage in last 48h and reduced visible spend. Finance flagged a mismatch on the March invoice vs raw cloud bill.

Maya Lin: Oh no. Do we know whether the credits were intentionally mapped to the pool or incorrectly attributed at ingest? :eyes:

billing-bot: NOTICE: Credit application detected. Credit source=partner:benchlabs applied to resource=lp-gpu-west. Credit_id=crd-2026-03-bl-77. Link: https://billing.redwood/credits/crd-2026-03-bl-77

Diego Torres: Quick summary from cloud export: credits show up as negative charges tied to `account_id=acct-partners` but our ingestion rule merged credit rows into pool-level charge buckets when `pool` field present. That caused partner credit to zero out internal dev charges.

Liam O'Connor: Not good. That means partner is effectively subsidizing our internal experiment costs. Need immediate correction and audit. Maya, can you run a scoped export for 2026-03-13..2026-03-15 for lp-gpu-west where credit_tag LIKE '%benchlabs%'?

Maya Lin: On it. SQL: ```SELECT usage_ts, account_id, pool, charge_usd, credit_id, credit_source FROM billing_raw WHERE pool='lp-gpu-west' AND credit_source LIKE '%benchlabs%' AND usage_ts BETWEEN '2026-03-13' AND '2026-03-15';```

ops-bot: ALERT: Billing ingest rule `merge_credits_to_pool` changed on 2026-03-12 by infra-tagging-service. More info: https://infra.redwood/changelog#merge_credits_to_pool

Maya Lin: Exported CSV to s3://redwood-costs/tmp/benchlabs-credit-audit-2494005012.csv and added a preview to the thread. Short stats: 1) total credit amount = $5,120.00 2) credited against acct-playground = $3,800 3) acct-devcore = $1,120 4) no customer acct affected (verified `acct-` prefixes)

Diego Torres: Thanks. Proposed remediation options: A) reverse the credit application and reapply to partner ledger (creates partner-facing credit memo) B) keep credit but create internal reallocation journal moving $4,920 from partner to infra-operational (so internal teams still charged) C) run a partial refund to affected internal teams and leave partner credit for their account.

Liam O'Connor: Finance prefers option A + journal audit trail. We should not let partner credits subsidize internal usage unless explicitly contracted. Maya, can you produce CSV formatted as `billing_id, original_account, new_account, amount_usd, reason` for the reversal?

Maya Lin: Will do. I filtered out any rows where `account_id LIKE 'cust-%'`. Uploading to s3 now and will DM Diego and Liam.

billing-bot: SUGGESTION: Create a credit policy rule to require `credit_owner` field on partner credits; if absent, mark credit as `hold` and route to #finance-partner-review. Filed ticket FIN-827.

Diego Torres: Also recommend a small change to ingestion: do not merge negative credit rows into pool-level aggregates. Keep credits as separate ledger line item with `credit_owner` metadata. I'll open infra ticket INF-1942 and link here.

Liam O'Connor: We also need a short narrative for the partner team so their account managers don't get surprised. Maya, add a one-paragraph explanation we can send to partnerships: what happened, what we changed, and the proposed partner-facing journal/credit note.

Maya Lin: Drafted and pasted below: "We detected an ingest rule regression where partner credits with source 'benchlabs' were collapsed into pool-level charges for low-priority GPU usage, which unintentionally offset internal team costs. We're reversing the credit application and issuing a corrected credit memo to BenchLabs. There will be no net charge impact to BenchLabs; internal allocations will be adjusted and a full audit trail provided."

Liam O'Connor: Good. Diego, once we have the CSV, can infra run the reverse in sandbox and provide a migration plan for production? Need playbook steps and an ETA.

Diego Torres: Plan: 1) run reverse script in sandbox against synthetic data (INF-1942) 2) dry-run the SQL reversal in billing_staging: ```INSERT INTO credit_reversals (billing_id, amount_usd, reversal_ts, reason) SELECT billing_id, -charge_usd, current_timestamp(), 'benchlabs misapplied' FROM billing_raw WHERE credit_source LIKE '%benchlabs%' AND pool='lp-gpu-west' AND usage_ts BETWEEN '2026-03-13' AND '2026-03-15';``` 3) once reviewed, apply to prod during maintenance window (2h) 4) create partner credit memo and notify partnerships. ETA 24-36h after approval.

Maya Lin: Uploaded final CSV s3://redwood-costs/audit/benchlabs-reversal-2494005012.csv and created PR for the partner note. Also updated FIN-827 with proposed policy text.

billing-bot: REMINDER: Approval required from @Liam O'Connor + @Jon Reyes for partner credit reversal.

Liam O'Connor: I'll approve once Diego confirms sandbox dry-run logs look correct and finance ledger entries are ready. Jon, can you weigh in on whether we need a manual journal entry instead of automated reversal?

Diego Torres: Sandbox dry-run in progress, will post logs to INF-1942 in ~2h. No automated reversal until approvals.

Maya Lin: Noted. Also adding short runbook snippet to infra-runbooks: 1) query credits by `credit_source` 2) verify `credit_owner` metadata 3) if misapplied, create reversal CSV and route to #finance for approval.

Liam O'Connor: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after INF-1942 results. :thumbsup:
